summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update33.json → valid=true). Precision correction plus an evidence bound for the heartbeat-admission finding, recorded as a correction of the existing knowledge id (with changed_premise, affected_uses empty since that revision records no uses) and a successor interpretation. Precisely: the admission window's second test compares the message's protocol-version field with the local configured protocol version minus one (raft.go:56-67; the comment frames the policy as dropping protocol zero from version two onward and supporting one version back), so what the fast path honours while the general path refuses is a peer whose protocol-version field falls outside that window — for a node at protocol three, a speaker of protocol zero or one — not 'an old release' as the earlier wording could be read. That narrows the affected population considerably (peers from the pre-protocol-two era) while leaving the mechanism unchanged: the heartbeat handler applies no version check so those heartbeats still adopt terms, record the sender as leader and refresh contact, and the timeout that would end the pin never fires. The evidence bound is separate and material: the retained compatibility module requires a previous-version dependency and replaces it with a relative directory that is absent from the captured snapshot (raft-compat/go.mod:20-29), so the rolling-upgrade and pre-vote pairings cannot be built from the snapshot and their coverage of any protocol gap is not decidable from the retained material — a property of the snapshot, not of the target code. Both points keep the conclusion conditional: mechanism source-established, affected population small, and the retained tests neither exercise nor exclude the precondition. Counterevidence preserved (the window deliberately accepts one protocol version back; narrowing weakens practical severity; the compat module's unbuildability adds no defect; nothing was executed).
